title: Sundial for your place
summary: your place, your wall: brass on slate
description: A horizontal garden dial or a vertical wall dial, also for a wall that does not face south, drawn for your latitude and longitude so that it reads the clock time of your zone: a brass plate and gnomon to laser cut and engrave, on a slate slab.
process: Laser cutting of brass sheet (the parts drawn as the beam's path), or waterjet with the kerf set to 0 and the machine's compensation; engraving by fibre laser or rotary cutter, filled with black wax; silver-soldered gnomon; slate slab from a stone supplier

difficulty.rationale: Data-driven lines for any plane dial with a thick gnomon, shadow assertions built from vectors, the beam path with its kerf and a one-way registration across two exports.

standards: C. Sabanski, The Sundial Primer (mysundial.ca), pages Horizontal Sundial and Vertical Declining Sundial: X = atan(sin lat tan h); SH = asin(cos d cos lat); SD = atan(sin d / tan lat); X = atan(cos lat tan h / (cos d + sin d sin lat tan h)) (read)
British Sundial Society, How sundials work, part 4: two styles on a thick gnomon, the noon gap, the other style before 6 a.m. and after 6 p.m. (read)
Wikipedia, Schema for vertical declining dials (after Waugh, Sundials: Their Theory and Construction, pp. 78-79): SD, SH and DL with cot DL = cot D sin(latitude) (read; Waugh himself not read)
NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory, General Solar Position Calculations: equation of time and time offset (read)
Wikipedia, Axial tilt: mean obliquity at J2000.0, 23 deg 26 min 21.406 s (read)
Wikidata P625 coordinates of the twelve cities (read 2026-11-09); their standard UTC offsets (CET +1, GMT 0, EST -5, JST +9) are common knowledge, not read
ISO 273 clearance holes, normal series: M4 4.5 mm, M5 5.5 mm, M6 6.6 mm (read from a chart labelled ISO 273, Albany County Fasteners)
Deutsches Kupferinstitut, CuZn37 data sheet (2005): density 8.44 g/cm3, expansion 19e-6 per K (read)
materials: Brass sheet CuZn37 (CW508L), 1.5 to 5 mm, for the dial plate and the gnomon (8.44 g/cm3)
Black engraving wax or paint for the lines
Silver solder (or soft solder indoors) for the gnomon's tabs
Slate slab (pedestal, 25 mm) or plaque (wall, 20 mm) with a 4 mm bevel
Two M4 brass screws with plugs (M5 in 5 mm sheet); four M6 screws for a wall plaque
Flexible adhesive to bed the plate
